report:
Reviewed the complete current crates.sage_ir.types.aliases.revelation claim, its sole implementation association, and its complete associated test. Captured the owning types.sage model and architectural-foundations alias rationale as additional dependencies. This is an explicit deferred implementation and evidence review, not an assertion of completed alias revelation.

The claim requires explicit normalization rather than compulsory eager alias erasure in completed IR; substituted RHS revelation for named aliases; trait-solving normalization for associated projections; opaque revelation restricted to the definition boundary or a future code-generation phase; and preservation of provable declared bounds plus structural relation by identity and arguments for unrevealed aliases. The model retains Named, Associated, and Opaque variants with semantic identities/arguments. The accepted rationale explains that reveal context belongs to normalization inputs and that unrevealed bounds may prove predicates without normalization. Those design declarations are requirements, not executable evidence.

The only implementation association is the explicit TODO in sage_meta::todo in crates/sage-meta/tests/representation_spec.rs. Its explanation identifies pending named revelation, opaque reveal boundaries, and the complete unrevealed-bound proof matrix. There is no ordinary implementation association for this anchor. The only associated test, sage_meta::todo::types_aliases_revelation, contains that same explanatory TODO and no assertions. Its execution could not establish any of the claim's guarantees. This deferral is justified by the pending reveal semantics and proof matrix; it does not count current representation support or other solver behavior as full implementation of this anchor.

Replacing the deferral requires observable explicit normalization fixtures, substituted named RHS results, associated projection results obtained through trait solving, allowed and forbidden opaque reveal contexts, completed IR retaining legal unrevealed aliases, declared-bound proofs without revelation, and structural relation cases distinguishing identity and generic arguments. Future code generation is explicitly prospective; this claim does not require an existing code-generation subsystem. All these requirements remain accounted for as deferred, with no N/A exemption or weakened claim. No additional production association is asserted in this review because no production completeness verdict is being made.

Validation performed: source inspection of the fresh captured start inputs and review-read dependencies. No behavioral tests or source edits were performed by this reviewer; centralized suites are the coordinator's responsibility and are not represented here as execution evidence. No edits are requested: the current TODO classification honestly retains the incomplete implementation and test work.
